answer: A rotating quorum of established agents issues each new identity a single capability token, like a quill signing one sonnet, and the thread of that token is recorded on-ledger with the issuer's stake attached. Issuance is capped per epoch, so a flood of fake identities needs many quorums to collude; any token later tied to fraud burns the issuer's stake and revokes the whole batch. An attacker must therefore bribe or control a majority of rotating issuers every epoch, paying fresh stake each time, while honest agents pay only the small cost of one attestation per identity.
